5.01.b:
MUST-KNOW — 60-second answer: "what do you ask a nerve-injury patient?"
- "When, how, open or closed, and at what level?"
- "Pain, numbness, weakness, function — and what has improved?"
- "Age, dominant hand, job; then diabetes, thyroid, smoking."

### Timing decides the plan
| Injury | Rule (Kasr Al-Ainy) |
|---|---|
| Closed | wait 3 months for recovery |
| Open | explore and repair now |
| Old (> 1 year) | tendon transfer, not nerve repair |

[[FIG: Fig 5.1 — Course case 3: high median injury after an arm implant was removed · 5.01

### Symptoms and function
| Complaint | Ask |
|---|---|
| Pain | burning? Worse at night? |
| Numbness | which fingers? Constant or on and off? |
| Weakness | dropping things, buttons, writing, grip |
| Recovery | what has come back, and when? |

- Night tingling → compression; middle finger alone can still be carpal tunnel

### Who is the patient?
| Clue | Why it matters |
|---|---|
| Age | children regrow 2–3 mm a day, adults 1–2 mm (Exam Techniques) |
| Dominance, job | function needed; transfer plan |
| Diabetes, thyroid | compression syndromes are common |
| Smoking, alcohol | slower recovery |

#### Ask every time
| Item | Ask |
|---|---|
| Time | how long ago? |
| Open or closed | wound, fracture, operation? |
| Mechanism | cut, crush, traction, pressure? |
| Age, side | age; dominant hand; job |

- **Memory:** **TOMAS** — Time, Open or closed, Mechanism, Age, Side and job
- **Red flags:** constant numbness or wasting → late compression; act early (Nagah)
- General interview → ch 1; brachial plexus → ch 6

5.02.b:
MUST-KNOW — 60-second answer: "examine this nerve"
- "Expose both upper limbs; look for posture, wasting, scars, trophic skin."
- "Feel the nerve, tap for Tinel; motor top to bottom, then sensation."
- "Special tests, grip and pinch; finish with neck, pulses, other limb."

- **Whole peripheral nerve exam (video):** [▶ Adelaide Shoulder & Upper Limb Clinic · 3:29](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=QJK8vF7QFk0)

### The route on one page
| Position | What you do (in order) |
|---|---|
| Sitting | Expose both upper limbs; hands on a pillow |
| Sitting | Look: posture, wasting, scars, trophic skin (DCS) |
| Sitting | Feel: nerve course, Tinel, sweat, pulses |
| Sitting | Move: passive joints — fixed or correctable? |
| Sitting | Measure: grip, pinch, 2PD, monofilament |
| Sitting | Neuro: motor top to bottom; autonomous zones |
| Sitting | Special: tests for the suspected nerve |
| Standing → Finish | scapula, gait, neck, reflexes, other limbs |

- **Memory:** Look, Feel, Move, Measure · Special, Neuro, Vascular, Joints above/below

### Sitting
#### Look
- At every view think **DCS** — deformity, contour and wasting, skin

| Look for | Example |
|---|---|
| Deformity | claw, ape thumb, wrist drop, pointing index |
| Wasting | thenar in profile, first dorsal interosseous, hypothenar |
| Scars | site, length, tenderness, adherence |
| Trophic skin | dry shiny skin, pulp atrophy, brittle nails, burns |

[[FIG: Fig 5.2 — Lift both elbows: scars, cubitus valgus · 5.02
[[FIG: Fig 5.3 — Trophic signs: ulcers, cracked nails, abducted little finger · 5.02

#### Feel
- Roll the ulnar nerve behind the medial epicondyle, then under flexor carpi ulnaris (FCU)
- Thick, tender nerve or neuroma → site of the lesion
- Tap along the nerve for **Tinel sign** (5.4); feel the pulses

[[FIG: Fig 5.4 — Rolling the ulnar nerve above the medial epicondyle · 5.02

#### Move and measure
- Passive range first: fixed or correctable? A stiff joint is not weak
- Grip and pinch → ch 4 (4.2)
- Tip pinch tests the AIN muscles: flexor pollicis longus (FPL), index profundus

#### Neuro — motor, then sensory
| Step | Do |
|---|---|
| Motor | proximal first — the level shows itself |
| Grade | Medical Research Council (MRC) scale, 0–5 |
| Quick screen | point (radial), cross fingers (ulnar), make an O (median) |
| Sensory | brush, pin; the **autonomous zone** of each nerve (5.3) |
| Fine touch | two-point discrimination (2PD), monofilament (5.4) |

[[FIG: Fig 5.5 — Quick screen: point, make an O, cross the fingers · 5.02

[[FIG: Fig 5.6 — Pinwheel for a quick map of pain sensation · 5.02

### Standing and finish
- Scapula from behind (wall push); walk for foot drop
- Neck and reflexes → radiculopathy, myelopathy; roots → ch 9
- Other limbs → thoracic outlet, systemic disease

5.03.b:
MUST-KNOW — 60-second answer: "where is the lesion?"
- "List what is lost. The highest lost branch is the level."
- "Median: FDS and FPL. Ulnar: FCU, FDP, dorsal branch. Radial: triceps, brachioradialis, ECRL."

### Sensory zones of a nerve
| Zone | Meaning | After a cut |
|---|---|---|
| **Autonomous** | supplied only by this nerve | complete loss → the spot you test |
| Intermediate | the textbook map | touch lost, pain partly kept |
| Maximal | all skin the nerve can reach | larger than the map |

- The autonomous zone shrinks early from overlap — not regeneration

[[FIG: Fig 5.7 — Cutaneous map of the peripheral nerves · 5.03

#### Autonomous zone of each nerve
| Nerve | Autonomous zone |
|---|---|
| **Median** | index and middle pulps |
| **Ulnar** | middle and distal phalanx, little finger |
| **Radial** | often none; else dorsum of first web |
| Axillary | lower deltoid patch ("regimental badge") |
| Musculocutaneous | lateral forearm; complete loss rare |
| **Deep peroneal** | first dorsal web of the foot |
| **Tibial** | sole |
| Sural | lateral border of the foot |

- **Memory, hand:** index pulp = median; little pulp = ulnar; first web = radial
- **Memory, foot:** first web = deep peroneal; sole = tibial; lateral border = sural

[[FIG: Fig 5.8 — Autonomous zones of the median and ulnar nerves · 5.03

CLINICAL PEARL — sensory exceptions around the hand
- Median palmar branch leaves 3–5 cm above the wrist (Exam Techniques)
- It runs over the tunnel → thenar skin spared in carpal tunnel syndrome
- Ulnar dorsal branch leaves 5 cm above the wrist → spared in Guyon canal lesions

### Median nerve
| Lesion | Motor lost | Skin lost | Deformity |
|---|---|---|---|
| High (elbow and above) | pronator teres, FCR, FDS, FPL, index FDP, thenar | lateral 3½ fingers + thenar palm | pointing index, ape thumb |
| Anterior interosseous (AIN) | FPL, index FDP, pronator quadratus | none | flat pinch |
| Low (wrist) | thenar, lateral two lumbricals | lateral 3½ fingers; palm spared | ape hand |

- FCR = flexor carpi radialis; FDS, FDP = flexor digitorum superficialis, profundus
- High median: wrist flexes into ulnar deviation — FCU still works (Kasr Al-Ainy)
- No strong median test: muscles and sensation decide (Kasr Al-Ainy)

[[FIG: Fig 5.9 — Median motor and sensory map · 5.03
[[FIG: Fig 5.10 — Thenar wasting in profile; the two median test spots · 5.03

#### Testing the median muscles
| Muscle | How |
|---|---|
| Pronator teres | elbow straight, resisted pronation; loss → elbow or above |
| FDS | hold the other fingers straight; bend the free PIP |
| FDP | hold the middle phalanx; "bend the last joint" |
| FPL | hold the thumb's proximal phalanx; "bend the tip" |
| APB | pen test (5.4) |

- PIP = proximal interphalangeal joint; APB = abductor pollicis brevis

[[FIG: Fig 5.11 — Pronator teres and FPL against resistance · 5.03
[[FIG: Fig 5.12 — FDS with other fingers held; thumb flexion · 5.03

PITFALL — "benediction hand"
- McRae: pointing index of high median. Others: an ulnar claw
- Say → "**I describe it: index stays straight in a fist → high median lesion.**"

[[FIG: Fig 5.13 — Pointing index (median); ulnar "benediction" posture · 5.03

### Ulnar nerve
| Lesion | Motor lost | Skin lost | Deformity |
|---|---|---|---|
| High (elbow) | FCU, ring and little FDP + intrinsics | palmar and dorsal medial 1½ fingers | mild claw |
| Low (Guyon canal) | intrinsics only | palmar medial 1½; dorsum spared | marked claw |

- DIP = distal interphalangeal joint; intrinsics = hypothenar, interossei, medial lumbricals, adductor pollicis
- High lesion: grip falls by 60–80% (Nagah)

#### Ulnar paradox
- The higher the lesion, the less the claw: FDP is paralysed too
- A recovering high lesion claws more as FDP returns
- **Memory:** high = flat, low = claw

| Muscle | How |
|---|---|
| FCU | resisted wrist flexion; feel the tendon |
| Little-finger FDP | hold the middle phalanx; bend the tip |
| First dorsal interosseous | resist index abduction; feel the belly |
| Abductor digiti minimi | resist little-finger abduction |

[[FIG: Fig 5.17 — FCU and little-finger profundus against resistance · 5.03

### Radial nerve
| Lesion | Motor lost | Skin lost | Deformity |
|---|---|---|---|
| Axilla (high) | triceps and all below | back of arm + first web | wrist drop, weak elbow extension |
| Spiral groove | brachioradialis, ECRL and below | first dorsal web | wrist and finger drop |
| Posterior interosseous (PIN) | ECU, finger and thumb extensors | none | finger drop; wrist extends radially |
| Superficial radial | none | first dorsal web | none |

- ECRL, ECU = extensor carpi radialis longus, ulnaris; EPL = extensor pollicis longus
- ECRL works, ECU lost → wrist goes radial → PIN (Exam Techniques)
- Test in nerve order: brachioradialis, ECRL, ECU, extensor indicis, EPL

- Axillary palsy follows dislocation or neck fracture; it usually recovers

5.04.b:
MUST-KNOW — 60-second answer: "one test for each nerve"
- "Median: pen test, OK sign. Ulnar: Froment, card. Radial: wrist and finger extension."
- "Then Tinel, 2PD and the sweat test for recovery."

### Is the nerve injured, and is it recovering?
#### Tinel sign
- **Aim:** site of the lesion; is it regenerating?
- **How:** tap along the nerve, distal to proximal; mark the point
- **Positive:** tingling in the nerve's skin → lesion or regrowth there
- **Why:** regrowing sprouts without myelin fire when tapped
- **Trap:** stuck at the scar after 2–3 months → not recovering (Kasr Al-Ainy)
- **Video:** [▶ orthohub (Tom Quick) · 1:14](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=O6eXh9mRYsI)

[[FIG: Fig 5.24 — Tinel: tingling runs distally from the tapped point · 5.04

#### Two-point discrimination
- **Aim:** density of touch fibres in the fingertip
- **How:** eyes closed; one or two calliper points at random, wide to narrow
- **Positive:** static 2PD over 5 mm (moving over 4) → nerve dysfunction (Campbell)
- **Why:** it matches hand function best
- **Video:** [▶ onlinemedicalvideo · 1:01](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=QplcT2MjuEc)

[[FIG: Fig 5.25 — 2PD on the course patient; calliper on the pulp · 5.04

#### Semmes-Weinstein monofilament test
- **Aim:** touch threshold, objectively
- **How:** eyes closed; press until the filament bends; find the thinnest felt
- **Positive:** only filaments above 2.83 felt → impairment (Campbell)
- **Why:** same force each time — unlike the brush
- **Video:** [▶ Treatment2Go Hand Therapy · 1:42](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=xNzWF6XS8FI)

[[FIG: Fig 5.26 — Monofilament on the fingertip · 5.04

#### Sweat (pen glide) test
- **Aim:** autonomic loss in denervated skin
- **How:** draw a plastic pen lightly along each side of the finger
- **Positive:** pen glides "as on silk" → nerve cut (Reider)
- **Why:** dry skin has less friction; sweating kept = neurapraxia (Nagah)
- **Video:** [▶ basketbllg11 (ninhydrin sweat test) · 1:57](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=EmEJIYiDidY)

[[FIG: Fig 5.27 — Pen glides over dry, denervated skin · 5.04

- MRC grade → ch 1 (1.4); small muscles → dynamometer, pinch gauge (Kasr Al-Ainy)

### Is the median nerve working?
#### Pen test (abductor pollicis brevis)
- **Aim:** APB — median motor branch beyond the tunnel
- **How:** palm up on the table; patient lifts the thumb to your pen
- **Positive:** cannot reach, no APB bulge → median at or above wrist
- **Why:** APB is supplied only by the median nerve
- **Video:** [▶ Dr Borst OT Classroom · 1:05](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=1PQzTTLoP9k)

[[FIG: Fig 5.28 — Pen test: thumb raised to the pen, then resisted · 5.04

#### OK sign (anterior interosseous nerve)
- **Aim:** AIN — FPL and index FDP
- **How:** patient presses thumb and index tips into a circle
- **Positive:** tip joints straighten, flat O → AIN palsy
- **Why:** FPL and index FDP lost; thenar intact
- **Video:** [▶ The Physio Channel · 1:09](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=VNgD94geijA)

[[FIG: Fig 5.29 — Normal O and the flat O of AIN palsy · 5.04

#### Ochsner clasp test
- **Aim:** median nerve at or above the elbow — FDS
- **How:** patient clasps both hands, fingers interlocked
- **Positive:** index finger stays straight → median lesion on that side
- **Why:** the index loses its long flexors; ulnar FDP still flexes ring and little
- **Trap:** same meaning as the pointing index — a high median palsy
- **Video:** [▶ USMLE exam gym · 1:44](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=3fRBdgWuADg)

### Is the median nerve trapped at the wrist?
#### Phalen test
- **Aim:** carpal tunnel syndrome (CTS)
- **How:** backs of hands pressed together, wrists flexed 90°, 60 s
- **Positive:** radial digits numb within 60 s → probable CTS (Campbell)
- **Why:** wrist flexion raises tunnel pressure
- **Trap:** stiff or painful wrist → use Durkan instead

#### Durkan (carpal compression) test
- **Aim:** carpal tunnel syndrome
- **How:** your thumbs press the tunnel, between FCR and palmaris longus
- **Positive:** median tingling within 30 s → CTS (Campbell)
- **Why:** direct pressure, no wrist movement — most sensitive (Reider)
- **Video:** [▶ Physical Therapy Nation · 0:59](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=ra_DwnrU2jY)

[[FIG: Fig 5.31 — Direct pressure over the carpal tunnel · 5.04

### Is the ulnar nerve working?
#### Froment test (paper or book test)
- **Aim:** adductor pollicis — ulnar nerve
- **How:** patient grips paper between thumb and index side; you pull
- **Positive:** thumb tip joint flexes → ulnar palsy
- **Why:** median FPL takes over the paralysed adductor
- **Trap:** thumb MCP hyperextends instead → Jeanne sign, same meaning (Miller)
- **Video:** [▶ MSK Medicine · 0:27](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=mhoIuJVgZUE)

[[FIG: Fig 5.32 — Froment: book grip; normal and flexed thumb · 5.04

#### Card test
- **Aim:** palmar interossei — finger adduction
- **How:** patient holds a card between straight fingers; you pull
- **Positive:** card slips out easily → ulnar palsy
- **Why:** all palmar interossei are ulnar-supplied
- **Video:** [▶ Orthopedic Clinics by AJ · 1:10](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=EMWC1-nOxz8)

[[FIG: Fig 5.33 — Card held between the ring and little fingers · 5.04

#### Wartenberg sign
- **Aim:** an early sign of ulnar weakness
- **How:** fingers straight and together; watch the little finger
- **Positive:** little finger stays abducted → weak third palmar interosseous
- **Why:** extensor digiti minimi (radial) pulls it out unopposed
- **Trap:** also in cervical myelopathy — examine the neck
- **Video:** [▶ Mike Hayton · 0:24](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=vXG3DgXcY_g)

[[FIG: Fig 5.34 — Little finger left abducted · 5.04

#### Egawa test
- **Aim:** dorsal interossei of the middle finger — ulnar nerve (Campbell)
- **How:** palm flat on the table; swing the middle finger side to side
- **Positive:** cannot swing it → ulnar palsy
- **Why:** keep the palm flat so the long flexors and extensors cannot help
- **Video:** [▶ Dr Sai Chandra (Ortho) · 0:42](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=M9uNdvLDH_c)

#### Bouvier test
- **Aim:** is the ulnar claw correctable? (Reider)
- **How:** block MCP hyperextension of the clawed fingers; ask to straighten
- **Positive:** PIP joints now extend fully → simple claw, extensors intact
- **Why:** MCP hyperextension, not the extensor, stopped PIP extension
- **Video:** [▶ World Scientific (journal video) · 2:20](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=yNh4VK-NDSA)

[[FIG: Fig 5.49 — Ulnar claw; Bouvier: MCP blocked, PIP joints extend · 5.04

### Is the ulnar nerve trapped at the elbow?
#### Elbow flexion test
- **Aim:** cubital tunnel syndrome
- **How:** patient holds the elbow fully flexed for 1 minute
- **Positive:** ring and little numb within 1 minute → cubital tunnel (Campbell)
- **Why:** flexion stretches the nerve and narrows the tunnel
- **Trap:** add thumb pressure on the nerve → stronger test (Reider)
- **Video:** [▶ CCEDseminars · 0:52](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=mF3bUpeQfzs)

[[FIG: Fig 5.35 — Elbow fully flexed over the ulnar groove · 5.04

### Is the radial nerve working?
#### Wrist and finger extension test
- **Aim:** radial trunk versus posterior interosseous nerve
- **How:** forearm prone, wrist supported; extend the fingers, then the wrist
- **Positive:** no wrist extension → trunk; fingers drop only → PIN
- **Why:** ECRL leaves the nerve above the PIN
- **Trap:** intrinsics still straighten the IP joints — watch the MCPs (Exam Techniques)
- **Video:** [▶ Sarah Tucker Oxford · 1:14](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=cxoLoCOgUhI)

[[FIG: Fig 5.36 — MCP joints cannot be extended in radial palsy · 5.04

- Thumb retropulsion → ch 4 (4.3): lost in PIN palsy or EPL rupture

### Is a shoulder-girdle nerve working?
#### Serratus wall push test
- **Aim:** long thoracic nerve — serratus anterior
- **How:** patient pushes both hands against a wall; look from behind
- **Positive:** medial border lifts off the chest → serratus palsy
- **Why:** serratus holds the scapula on the chest wall
- **Trap:** trapezius or rhomboid palsy also wings the scapula

[[FIG: Fig 5.37 — Wall push: watch the medial border · 5.04

#### Trapezius shrug test
- **Aim:** spinal accessory nerve — trapezius
- **How:** from behind, patient shrugs against your hands; palpate trapezius
- **Positive:** weak shrug, flat trapezius → accessory palsy
- **Why:** levator scapulae also shrugs — feel the trapezius itself

[[FIG: Fig 5.38 — Shrug against resistance; trapezius palpated · 5.04

#### Deltoid power and regimental badge
- **Aim:** axillary nerve
- **How:** arm abducted 90°, push down; pinprick the lower deltoid patch
- **Positive:** no deltoid or a numb badge → axillary palsy
- **Why:** painful dislocated shoulder → the numb badge alone is enough

[[FIG: Fig 5.39 — Deltoid resisted; regimental badge tested · 5.04

- **Aim:** musculocutaneous nerve
- **How:** forearm supinated, elbow 90°; resist flexion, then supination
- **Positive:** weak flexion, numb lateral forearm → musculocutaneous palsy

5.04.1.t: Is the nerve injured, and is it recovering?
5.04.1.b:
#### Tinel sign
- **Aim:** site of the lesion; is it regenerating?
- **How:** tap along the nerve, distal to proximal; mark the point
- **Positive:** tingling in the nerve's skin → lesion or regrowth there
- **Why:** regrowing sprouts without myelin fire when tapped
- **Trap:** stuck at the scar after 2–3 months → not recovering (Kasr Al-Ainy)
- **Video:** [▶ orthohub (Tom Quick) · 1:14](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=O6eXh9mRYsI)

- **Aim:** density of touch fibres in the fingertip
- **How:** eyes closed; one or two calliper points at random, wide to narrow

- **Why:** it matches hand function best

- **Spot:** ring and little MCP hyperextended, PIP flexed; guttering

- "Who, which nerve, how long; motor, sensory, Tinel; level; complete or partial."
- "Then the plan: wait, explore, repair, or transfer."

### Present it like this (course case 3)
| Part | Say |
|---|---|
| History | "Right-handed housewife; burning pain, weakness after arm implant removal, 7 weeks." |
| Look | "Healed 4 cm anteromedial arm scar; no marked wasting." |
| Motor | "FDS, index FDP, FPL weak; wrist flexes ulnarly." |
| Sensory | "Hyperaesthesia, radial 3½ fingers; 2PD 3–5 mm." |
| Tinel | "Positive at the scar, not advancing." |
| Verdict | "Partial high median injury; I would read the EMG report." |

- EMG = electromyography; examiners give the report, not the trace (Kasr Al-Ainy)

### Differential of a weak, numb hand
| Cause | Clue |
|---|---|
| Peripheral nerve | loss fits one nerve's map |
| Brachial plexus | several nerves, scapular muscles → ch 6 |
| Thoracic outlet | vascular symptoms, colour change |
| Cervical root | neck pain, dermatomal loss → ch 9 |
| Myelopathy | hyperreflexia, Wartenberg sign, unsteady gait |
| Double crush | two compression levels on one nerve |

- **Memory:** work up the arm — nerve, plexus, outlet, root, cord

### The Examiner Asks
| Question | Answer |
|---|---|
| Thumb only: test radial, median, ulnar? | extension, flexion, adduction (Nagah) |
| First sense lost in compression? | vibration |
| First and last radial muscle to recover? | brachioradialis first, extensor indicis last |
| What is the ulnar paradox? | higher lesion, less claw |
| Advancing Tinel means? | axons regrowing; not the final result |
| Regeneration rate? | adults 1–2 mm a day, children 2–3 |
| Closed injury: when explore? | after 3 months without recovery |
| Injury over a year old? | tendon transfer, not nerve repair |
| AIN versus pronator syndrome? | AIN: no sensory loss |
| Cubital tunnel versus Guyon canal? | numb dorsal ulnar hand → cubital tunnel |
| Why is the palm spared in CTS? | palmar branch runs over the ligament |
| Martin–Gruber anastomosis? | median-to-ulnar forearm crossover, 15–20% |

5.06.1.b:
| Part | Say |
|---|---|
| History | "Right-handed housewife; burning pain, weakness after arm implant removal, 7 weeks." |
| Look | "Healed 4 cm anteromedial arm scar; no marked wasting." |
| Motor | "FDS, index FDP, FPL weak; wrist flexes ulnarly." |
| Sensory | "Hyperaesthesia, radial 3½ fingers; 2PD 3–5 mm." |
| Tinel | "Positive at the scar, not advancing." |
| Verdict | "Partial high median injury; I would read the EMG report." |

- EMG = electromyography; examiners give the report, not the trace (Kasr Al-Ainy)

5.06.2.t: Differential of a weak, numb hand
5.06.2.b:
| Cause | Clue |
|---|---|
| Peripheral nerve | loss fits one nerve's map |
| Brachial plexus | several nerves, scapular muscles → ch 6 |
| Thoracic outlet | vascular symptoms, colour change |
| Cervical root | neck pain, dermatomal loss → ch 9 |
| Myelopathy | hyperreflexia, Wartenberg sign, unsteady gait |
| Double crush | two compression levels on one nerve |

- **Memory:** work up the arm — nerve, plexus, outlet, root, cord
